context:
Documentation, not code. The mechanism is correct; only its discoverability is missing.

Write the maintainer procedure into docs/operations/results-phase-2-runbook.md and cross-reference it from results-data/README.md:

- Withdrawing from the public archive: open a deletion-only PR against published-results. Cite #1882 and #1940 as the worked examples.
- Adding to the public archive: land on develop, then run `gh workflow run sync-results-data-to-published.yml` and merge the auto/results-mirror-* PR. Never add by hand.
- Why: name the union overlay and the four-signal waiver explicitly, so the next reader does not have to reverse-engineer them from the workflow.
- Ordering when a change both adds and deletes: mirror last, so the corpus floor is never violated on the public branch.

Do not relax the four-signal waiver to make hand-opened additions work. It is confined to an unforgeable bot identity on purpose; widening it would let a fork PR launder a community bundle into a ranking-eligible maintainer-run stamp.
description:
GAP found 2026-08-28 by hitting it: PR #1940's first revision failed CI, and the reason was only discoverable by reading validate-submission.yml line by line.

Two constraints exist, both deliberate, neither written down anywhere a maintainer would look:

1. DELETIONS never propagate. sync-results-data-to-published.yml applies a union overlay to results-data/bundles, precisely so an automated mirror can never delete public community content. A develop-side withdrawal therefore needs a separate hand-opened PR against published-results. PR #1882 (2026-08-24, 154 files) and PR #1940 both did this, but neither the runbook nor results-data/README.md says it is the procedure.

2. ADDITIONS by hand are impossible. The manifest waiver in validate-submission.yml requires four signals: base published-results, head.repo.fork == false, PR author github-actions[bot], and head_ref matching auto/results-mirror-*. A maintainer PR fails three of them, is treated as a community submission, and every added bundle is rejected for a missing sidecar. So a bundle can only reach published-results through the sync mirror.

The combined rule -- hand-opened PRs against published-results must be DELETION-ONLY, additions go through the mirror -- is nowhere stated. It cost a failed CI run and a full workflow read to recover, and the next person will pay the same cost.

Related but distinct from validate-submission-empty-bundle-arg-scans-live-corpus, which is the actual bug that made the failure confusing. Even with that bug fixed, constraint 2 stands.

preserves.behavior: The four-signal manifest waiver, including head.repo.fork == false as the unforgeable signal
The union overlay in sync-results-data-to-published.yml: an automated mirror must never delete public content

verifications.description: Runbook states the deletion-only rule for hand-opened published-results PRs
Runbook states additions must go through the mirror

work_units.summary: Write the deletion-only rule and the mirror-for-additions rule into the results phase 2 runbook
Name the union overlay and the four-signal waiver explicitly, citing #1882 and #1940
